questions.q: Why does restoring a database backup to a different server commonly create orphaned users?
options: Database users travel with the backup, but the matching server logins live in master on the original server and may not exist on the target
SQL Server automatically deletes all users during any restore operation
Orphaned users are created intentionally as a security precaution during restores
Restoring a backup always requires re-creating every table's permissions from scratch
questions.explain: Users are stored inside the database itself, but logins live in master — if the target server lacks a login with a matching sid, the user has nothing to map to.

questions.q: What defines an orphaned user in the real detection query against sys.database_principals?
options: A database user whose sid has no matching row in sys.server_principals
Any database user with a NULL default_schema_name
Any user that is a member of the db_owner role
A user whose name does not match any table name in the database
questions.explain: The join checks whether each database principal's sid exists among server principals — no match means orphaned.

questions.q: What is the modern, supported statement to remap an orphaned database user to an existing login?
options: ALTER USER ... WITH LOGIN
sp_change_users_login (recommended for all new scripts)
GRANT LOGIN TO USER
RESTORE USER ... WITH LOGIN
questions.explain: ALTER USER ... WITH LOGIN is the current, actively supported way to relink a database user to a server login.

questions.q: What is the status of sp_change_users_login according to this lesson?
options: It's legacy — it still works on many installations, but ALTER USER ... WITH LOGIN is the recommended approach
It was removed entirely starting with SQL Server 2016
It's the only way to fix orphaned users in contained databases
It's a brand-new procedure introduced to replace ALTER USER
questions.explain: sp_change_users_login predates ALTER USER ... WITH LOGIN and is documented as legacy, though it can still function.

questions.q: If the matching login does not yet exist at all on the target server, what must happen before ALTER USER ... WITH LOGIN can fix the orphaned user?
options: The login must be created first, matching the original SQL login's password or the Windows account
Nothing — ALTER USER can create the login automatically in every case
The entire database must be dropped and re-restored
The user must first be granted sysadmin
questions.explain: ALTER USER ... WITH LOGIN relinks a user to an existing login — if no matching login exists yet, it has to be created first.
